title: Ensemble Methods
text:
Ensemble Methods
Ensemble methods are widely used to represent probability distributions over states.
A simulation may estimate an observable as
\[
\langle A \rangle \approx \frac{1}{N} \sum_{n=1}^N A(x_n)
\]
This idea connects directly to Monte Carlo, importance sampling, and other numerical integration techniques.

title: Statistical Mechanics
text:
The canonical ensemble assigns probability
\[
P(x) = \frac{e^{-\beta E(x)}}{Z}
\]
where \(Z\) is the partition function.
This formalism underlies Monte Carlo, molecular simulation, and the study of equilibrium distributions.

title: Phase Transitions
text:
Phase Transitions
Phase transitions are changes in collective behavior as control parameters change.
A simple Ising-like model can illustrate competition between energy and entropy:
\[
H = -J \sum_{\langle i,j \rangle} s_i s_j
\]
The resulting behavior depends on temperature, geometry, and interaction strength.

title: Markov Chains
text:
Markov Chains
A Markov chain describes transitions between states with probabilities that depend only on the current state.
\[
P(X_{n+1}=j \mid X_n=i) = P_{ij}
\]
For a 2-state chain,
\[
P = \begin{pmatrix}
1-\alpha & \alpha \\
\beta & 1-\beta
\end{pmatrix}
\]
The long-time behavior of the chain depends on the structure of this matrix, especially the stationary distribution and mixing properties.

title: Stochastic Processes
text:
Stochastic Processes
A simple diffusion model can be written as
\[
\mathrm{d}X_t = \sqrt{2D}\,\mathrm{d}W_t.
\]
This form models a Brownian motion with diffusion coefficient \(D\).


Code
import numpy as np

D = 1.0
dt = 0.01
N = 2000

increments = np.sqrt(2 * D * dt) * np.random.randn(N)
trajectory = np.cumsum(increments)

print(trajectory[:10])
print(f"Mean displacement: {trajectory[-1]:.3f}")

title: Molecular Simulation
text:
Molecular simulation combines statistical mechanics with numerical integration to estimate system behavior.
The central challenge is to sample configurations from a distribution such as
\[
\pi(x) \propto e^{-\beta U(x)}.
\]
This supports methods such as Metropolis Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics.

title: Non-equilibrium Systems
text:
Non-equilibrium Systems
A non-equilibrium system is driven away from equilibrium by a gradient, forcing, or kinetic process.
Examples include:

diffusion with external drift
reaction-diffusion systems
driven lattice models
irreversible transport processes

The dynamics can often be expressed in terms of a flux or a drift-diffusion equation.

title: Measurement and Instrumentation
text:
Measurement and Instrumentation
Successful scientific work depends on disciplined measurement and careful interpretation.
A good measurement workflow typically contains:

calibration
data acquisition
signal processing
validation
interpretation

This is a natural companion to scientific computing and hardware experimentation.
